common.demoNotice: This roadmap uses demonstration data and is not an official determination. Confirm all requirements, fees, dates, and approvals with your municipality.
common.notFoundBody: This demonstration project is stored in this browser. It may have been cleared, or the link is from another device.

a11y.languageHint: Changes the words on screen. It does not change your permit steps.
a11y.note: These controls change display only. They do not change your permit roadmap.

graph.title: Permit graph
graph.subtitle: Each node is a department step. Arrows mean “cannot start until.” Colors follow status. A gold outline is a bottleneck. A dashed ring is the critical path.
graph.ethics: AI may later explain a cited passage. It cannot add a permit.
graph.selectHint: Select a step to see the evaluation trace that included it.
graph.noTrace: No evaluation trace is stored for this step.
graph.followUpNote: Deterministic template from rule trace — edit before sending; not an official filing.

tour.step1Body: Harbor Kitchen is stuck: the Health permit has been In Review for 12 days (gold outline), holding up Fire and the Business license.
tour.step1Cta: Click the gold Health permit node
tour.step2Body: Every permit comes from a versioned rule, matched intake fields, and model-code citations — never a language model guessing the law.
tour.step3Body: Click “Mark Approved → unlock next step” (or change the status dropdown) to clear the bottleneck, generate a department follow-up, and hand the next action to Fire.
tour.step3Cta: Click Mark Approved to test the ripple
tour.step4Body: Switch tabs to inspect itemized surcharges, one-click sample PDF uploads, and inspection pass criteria — all saved to your database workspace.

home.eyebrow: Permit Guide for Residents & Small Businesses
home.title: Know every permit, fee, and step before you apply.
home.lede: Starting a home food business, renovating a shop, or planning a community event? PermitPilot turns confusing city rules into a simple, step-by-step checklist, showing you what to file first, what it costs, and how long it takes.
home.noProjects: No projects yet. Answer a few questions and we will build your permit roadmap.
home.trySample: Try a sample, or create an account
home.sampleBlurb: No email needed. This opens three example projects so you can click around:
home.sampleCafe: Beacon Corner Cafe — a shop remodel
home.sampleParty: Wharf Street Block Party — an outdoor event
home.signupBlurb: After you create an account, we will ask a few questions and build a permit checklist for your project.
home.signinBlurb: If you do not have a project yet, we will ask a few questions first so the roadmap matches what you are building.
home.everything: Everything you can do on this website
home.everythingBody: You do not need to be a contractor or lawyer to figure out city permits. Here are the 6 tools included for every project:
home.trustTitle: Real rulebook logic — never a chatbot guessing
home.trustBody: Chatbots can make up city laws. PermitPilot uses a fixed checklist of town rules so you get the exact same permit steps, fee math, and rule links every time. (Note: Demo Harbor is a fictional sample town created for demonstration.)
home.g1title: Tell us what you are building or opening
home.g1does: Answer 3 simple questions about your project, like opening a home bakery, remodeling a shop, adding a room, or hosting a neighborhood event.
home.g1get1: Pick a ready-made example (Home Bakery, Corner Cafe, or Block Party) if you don't want to type.
home.g1get2: Instantly builds a custom checklist of every city permit you need.
home.g2title: See which permits come first (and what is holding you up)
home.g2does: Shows your permits as a step-by-step map so you never apply for the wrong permit first or get stuck waiting in the wrong line.
home.g2get1: Highlights any step that is slowing down your project in gold.
home.g2get2: Click any step to see a plain-English explanation of why the town requires it.
home.g2get3: Includes a ready-to-copy follow-up email you can send to the city department.
home.g3title: Track your progress and estimated dates
home.g3does: Gives you a realistic time range for each department review and updates your next recommended step as approvals come in.
home.g3get1: Mark steps as Not Started, Submitted, In Review, or Approved.
home.g3get2: See which permits you can work on at the same time to save weeks.
home.g4title: Keep all required documents in one place
home.g4does: Lists the exact files each department asks for, like a floor plan, menu, or food safety certificate, before you submit.
home.g4get1: Upload your own PDFs or photos, or click 'Attach sample PDF' to test how it works.
home.g4get2: Checks off each requirement as you go so nothing is missing.
home.g5title: See what your permits will cost upfront
home.g5does: Adds up the town’s permit fees based on your project size and work type so you can budget before spending money.
home.g5get1: Shows every fee line-by-line in plain numbers, no hidden math.
home.g6title: Pass your city inspections the first time
home.g6does: Gives you a simple pre-inspection checklist for Building, Fire, and Health before the inspector visits your site.
home.g6get1: Check off items as you prepare your space.
home.g6get2: Switch languages, Plain English, or High-Contrast mode anytime at the top of the page.

login.eyebrow: Sign In or Try a Sample Account
login.sampleTitle: Try our Sample Account (No Sign-Up Needed)
login.sampleBody: Want to see how PermitPilot works without creating an account? Click below to open a ready-made account with 3 example projects (a Home Bakery, a Corner Cafe, and a Neighborhood Block Party).
login.signInTitle: Sign in to save your projects
login.signInBody: If this is your first time, we will ask a few questions and build a checklist for your project.
login.signUpBody: Next we will ask a few questions about what you are opening or building, then create your permit roadmap.
login.savedNote: Your permit checklists, uploaded documents, and progress are saved automatically.

intake.welcomeEyebrow: Welcome — let’s set up your project
intake.welcomeTitle: A few questions so we can build your checklist
intake.welcomeBody: Tell us your state and what you’re opening. We’ll build a permit map for your restaurant, salon, shop, or event — not a sample business.
intake.presetsBody: Testing the rules engine? Pick a preset to pre-fill all 3 steps or generate the roadmap in one click.
intake.step1Body: Start with your state, then pick the closest match. This chooses which permits show up on your map.
intake.step2Body: Size, location, and the kind of work change fees and which departments get involved.
intake.kindOfSpace: What kind of space is this?
intake.remodeling: We are remodeling or adding space
intake.step3Body: Use your business, event, or project name. We’ll build the roadmap from the answers you already gave.
intake.foodServed: Food will be prepared or served
intake.beforeBody: Permit steps come from a fixed rulebook for your answers. Citations may be matched from downloaded {state} source files. This is a planning guide, not a legal determination.
intake.errState: Choose your state and the closest match for what you are opening.
intake.errSize: Enter the size of the space and a rough cost.
intake.errName: Give your project a name to continue.
